_meta.feast: Synaxis of All Saints of North America
_meta._source: OCA — https://www.oca.org/fs/commemoration-all-saints-north-america (Matins canon, Odes 3 and 6, verbatim). Register: 'tt' (transformed from OCA 'yy' source via scripts/yy-to-tt.js on 2026-06-19, with one hand-fix for 'didst provid' → 'didst provide'). Tone for the canon is not stated on the source page.
_meta._note: Used by the Liturgy Beatitudes (Third Antiphon) on Sun 6/14 via FEAST_BEATITUDES_OVERRIDES in server-lib/sources/beatitudes.js. Only Odes 3 and 6 are needed for the Beatitudes; the OCA page lists 4 troparia per ode but the Beatitudes layout uses 2 per ode (matching the existing Octoechos format), so the first two from each ode are populated here.

ode3.irmos: The Church of the Gentiles was like a desert, barren in its pagan ways, but now it has blossomed by Thy coming, O Lord; in that same coming my heart is confirmed.

troparia.text: Rejoice, land of Alaska, for the Orthodox Faith has been planted in thee and now bears the fruit of salvation throughout North America.
Let us praise in sacred hymns our Father Herman of Alaska, who has bestowed his blessing upon the New World and has left us his holy relics as a source of healing for many who honor his memory.

ode3.theotokion: Grant us the help of thy prayers, Most holy Lady, for our enemies have overwhelmed us. But through thee, All pure One, can we be delivered. Intercede with Thy Son that we may be saved.

ode6.irmos: Encompassed in the depths of sin, I entreat the unfathomable depths of Thy compassion: bring me out of corruption, O Lord.

troparia.text: We praise thee, O Holy Hierarch Innocent, for like the Apostles to the Slavs, Cyril and Methodius, thou didst leave thy homeland to journey to a foreign land. Following their example, thou didst enlighten thy new people by translating the Holy Scriptures into their own language.

O Holy Hierarch Tikhon, thou didst provide for the spiritual well-being of the Church in the New World by establishing the monastic tradition. Through thy prayers, may the monastery thou didst found in the mountains of Pennsylvania, named after thy heavenly patron, St. Tikhon of Zadonsk, be a haven for many who give all in their love of Christ.

ode6.theotokion: As thou hast continually interceded for our land, at the prayers of the North American Saints, look upon us now, O Most pure Theotokos, and, as the hope of the hopeless and helper of those in distress, grant us a sign of thy compassion, O Lady.
